content: 1. Immediate-release dosing: Administer 50–100 mg orally twice daily. 2. Extended-release tablets: Administer 1 mg/kg orally once daily for a duration of 12 weeks. 3. Community-acquired MRSA infections: Start with 200 mg orally as an initial dose, followed by 100 mg orally twice daily for 5–10 days. 4. Uncomplicated infections: Administer 100 mg orally every 12 hours for at least 7 days. 5. Uncomplicated infections in males (excluding anorectal infections or urethritis): Start with 200 mg orally as an initial dose, followed by 100 mg orally twice daily for at least 4 days. 6. Uncomplicated gonococcal urethritis in men: Administer 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 5 days. 7. Infections caused by Chlamydia trachomatis or Ureaplasma urealyticum: Administer 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 7 days. For more prolonged infections, continue therapy for 6–8 weeks. 8. Severe infections: Start with 200 mg orally as an initial dose, followed by 100 mg orally every 12 hours for 10–15 days. 9. Intravenous therapy for severe infections: Administer 100 mg intravenously twice daily for at least 5 weeks. 10. Renal impairment: Reduce the dose and/or frequency of administration as appropriate. 11. Pediatric use (<12 years): Safety and efficacy have not been established. For immediate-release products, administer 4 mg/kg orally as an initial dose (not exceeding 200 mg), followed by 2 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours (not exceeding 200 mg per day). For extended-release tablets, administer 1 mg/kg orally once daily for 12 weeks. 12. Pediatric use (≤8 years): Not recommended unless alternative antibiotics are not an option. 13. Pediatric use (>8 years): Administer 4 mg/kg orally or intravenously as an initial dose (not exceeding 200 mg), followed by 2 mg/kg every 12 hours (not exceeding the adult dose). Therapy duration is typically 5–10 days. Drug Interactions: 1. Minocycline and acitretin: Both drugs can increase intracranial pressure. This combination is contraindicated. 2. Minocycline and tretinoin: Co-administration increases the risk of intracranial pressure elevation. Avoid this combination. 3. Minocycline and aluminum hydroxide: Aluminum hydroxide reduces minocycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 4. Minocycline and aminolevulinic acid (oral): Co-administration increases phototoxicity risk. Avoid combining these drugs. 5. Minocycline and aminolevulinic acid (topical): Minocycline enhances the phototoxic effects of aminolevulinic acid. Avoid this combination. 6. Minocycline and amoxicillin: Minocycline may antagonize the bactericidal effects of amoxicillin. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely. 7. Minocycline and atracurium: Minocycline enhances the neuromuscular blocking effects of atracurium, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination. 8. Minocycline and BCG vaccine (live): Minocycline reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 9. Minocycline and calcium supplements (e.g., calcium acetate, calcium carbonate, calcium chloride): Calcium reduces minocycline absorption in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 10. Minocycline and cholera vaccine: Minocycline may inactivate the vaccine strain. Avoid administering the cholera vaccine within 14 days of systemic antibiotic use. 11. Minocycline and cisatracurium: Minocycline enhances the effects of cisatracurium, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. Avoid this combination. 12. Minocycline and dicloxacillin: Minocycline may antagonize the effects of dicloxacillin. Avoid co-administration or monitor closely. 13. Minocycline and ferrous sulfate: Iron supplements reduce minocycline absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours. 14. Minocycline and isotretinoin: Co-administration increases the risk of pseudotumor cerebri. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Minocycline and magnesium supplements (e.g., magnesium chloride, magnesium citrate): Magnesium reduces minocycline absorption. Avoid co-administration or separate doses by at least 2 hours.
